title: Correct Verdicts, Flawed Reasoning: Structured Auditing of LLM-based Vulnerability Reasoning
title_zh: 正确判定，错误推理：基于大型语言模型（LLM）的漏洞推理结构化审计

paragraphs.en: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed for automated software vulnerability analysis. Binary classification alone is often insufficient; practitioners need explanations to triage reported bugs and engineer patches. Standard practice relies on Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting to elicit such explanations. However, because CoT represents reasoning as free-form natural language, models can obscure logical leaps, hallucinated execution steps, and internal inconsistencies behind plausible prose, leading to correct verdict, flawed reasoning , such as reaching the correct verdict via a non-existent execution path. Our manual audit reveals that approximately 60 % 60\% of correct vulnerability verdicts are accompanied by these fabricated or unverifiable claims. Free-form explanations allow reasoning errors to evade LLM-as-a-judge evaluation.

paragraphs.en: To better audit LLM reasoning, we present V ulnerability E xplanation R easoning A uditor ( VERA ), an automated framework for auditing whether the explanation adheres to the source code; and whether it contains logical contradiction. Rather than accepting free-form text, VERA first asks models to output a Structured Reasoning Record (SRR), encoding the information necessary for vulnerability reasoning into machine-readable fields, including tracked pointers, memory operations, and state transitions. A multi-stage judge then audits each SRR against eight well-defined reasoning failure modes. Most stages use deterministic syntactic checks, with LLM calls reserved only when semantic interpretation is required. Furthermore, the standardized schema of SRRs enables automated mutation testing to benchmark reasoning judges at scale without human annotation. Our empirical evaluation demonstrates that reasoning flaws occur in correct verdicts just as frequently as in incorrect ones, and VERA exposes 87 % 87\% of reasoning errors that free-form LLM-as-judge systematically miss. VERA replaces blind trust in CoT prose with structured reasoning audits, filtering hallucinated vulnerability reports and pinpointing stage-specific failures.
paragraphs.zh: 为了更好地审计 LLM 推理过程，我们提出了漏洞解释推理审计器（VERA），这是一个自动化框架，用于审计解释是否符合源代码，以及是否存在逻辑矛盾。 VERA 不直接接受自由格式文本，而是首先要求模型输出结构化推理记录（SRR），将漏洞推理所需的信息编码为机器可读的字段，包括跟踪指针、内存操作和状态转换。 随后，一个多阶段裁判会对每个 SRR 依据八种明确定义的推理失败模式进行审计。 大多数阶段采用确定性的句法检查，仅在需要语义解释时才会调用 LLM。 此外，SRR 的标准化格式使得自动化变异测试成为可能，从而无需人工标注即可大规模评估推理裁判的性能。 我们的实证评估表明，正确判断中出现的推理缺陷频率与错误判断相当，而 VERA 能够揭示自由格式 LLM 裁判系统性地遗漏的 87% 的推理错误。 VERA 用结构化的推理审计取代了对 CoT 文本的盲目信任，从而过滤出虚构的漏洞报告，并精准定位各阶段的特定失败点。

paragraphs.en: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being adopted for automated vulnerability detection in software security ( Ding et al., 2025 ; Xu et al., 2025 ; Ságodi et al., 2024 ; Nong et al., 2026 ; Fang et al., 2024 ) . Trust in LLM-generated vulnerability assessments depends not only on the final verdict but also on the underlying reasoning, especially in security-critical settings ( Johnson et al., 2013 ; Lu et al., 2026 ) . Explanations of where and why a vulnerability exists help developers and security analysts validate findings and make informed patching and auditing decisions. However, LLMs may provide hallucinated explanations and justifications ( Ji et al., 2023 ) . A common LLM-based vulnerability analysis approach is to use unconstrained Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning in natural language. While flexible, free-form CoT allows models to produce plausible-sounding but fundamentally hallucinated justifications ( Lekssays et al., 2025 ; Geirhos et al., 2020 ; Pearce et al., 2022 ; Turpin et al., 2023 ; Lyu et al., 2023 ) , a phenomenon we refer to as “correct verdicts, flawed reasoning.”

paragraphs.en: For example, the program in Fig. 1(c) has a Use-After-Free (UAF) vulnerability (CWE-416 ( MITRE, 2024 ) ). A common way to explain the vulnerability is that when the reference count is zero (L12), the pointers e->name and e are freed on lines L13, 14, then the dereferencing e->name in audit_log (L16) leads to UAF. When prompted to identify and explain the vulnerability in this program, as illustrated in Fig. 1(a) , LLM via CoT correctly identified UAF, but its reasoning falsely assumes cache_remove frees e (L11) then dereferencing e->refs (L12) is the UAF. This error violates basic code adherence as the reasoning was based on the stale comment (L11) rather than actual implementation. Though not shown in the example, reasoning could also contain logical contradictions, such as explicitly identifying a vulnerability step-by-step only to conclude with a “Safe” final verdict.
paragraphs.zh: 例如，图 1(c) 中的程序存在使用后释放（Use-After-Free, UAF）漏洞（CWE-416 (MITRE, 2024)）。 解释该漏洞的一种常见方式是：当引用计数为零时（L12），指针 e->name 和 e 在 L13、L14 行被释放，随后在 audit_log（L16）中对 e->name 的解引用操作导致了 UAF。 当被要求识别并解释该程序中的漏洞时，如图 1(a) 所示，通过 CoT 的 LLM 正确识别出了 UAF，但其推理错误地假设 cache_remove 释放了 e（L11），因此对 e->refs（L12）的解引用操作就是 UAF。 这种错误违反了基本的代码遵循原则，因为其推理基于过时的注释（L11），而非实际的实现代码。 尽管示例中未展示，但推理也可能包含逻辑矛盾，例如明确地逐步识别出漏洞，却在最终结论中判定为“安全”。

paragraphs.en: Our manual review of free-form CoT reasoning generated by four state-of-the-art LLMs revealed that LLMs frequently provide explanations with hallucinated external knowledge ( 55 ​ - ​ 61 % 55\text{-}61\% factually incorrect) or unverifiable code assumptions ( 19 ​ - ​ 34 % 19\text{-}34\% ) (more details in Sec. 2 ). Relying on flawed explanations in production carries significant risk: engineers acting on hallucinated logic may write broken patches, while high benchmark accuracy conceals critical model failure modes (e.g., missing the actual UAF in Fig. 1(c) ). Addressing this requires a framework that checks whether underlying reasoning by the LLMs is both grounded in facts about the source code and are logically consistent.

paragraphs.en: The primary challenge of auditing LLM vulnerability reasoning is that free-form CoT reasoning lacks explicit structure and intermediate checkable steps, e.g., where pointers are freed and dereferenced. Furthermore, unlike algorithmic or boolean problems where intermediate logical steps unfold sequentially, checkable reasoning steps for vulnerability analysis need to be explicitly formalized and structured. Hence, recent efforts have turned to LLM-as-judge approaches ( Guo et al., 2026 ; Zhu et al., 2026 ; Lu et al., 2026 ) (Step II of Fig. 1(a) ); however, evaluating unstructured natural language with another neural model is still prone to hallucinations and yields no verifiable evidences. For instance, in Fig. 1(a) , the LLM-as-judge is likewise misled by the stale comment and misses the error. Human experts can detect such issues, but their review does not scale.

paragraphs.en: Our core insight is that for vulnerability analysis, checkable intermediate reasoning steps naturally correspond to program state transitions and that a broad spectrum of vulnerability classes, from memory safety to resource lifecycle errors, can be specified as state sequences. For instance, finding a UAF can be described as a process of finding operations that transition a pointer to Allocated state and then to Freed , and look for a dereference operation of any Freed pointer. In Fig. 1(c) , this sequence is e->refs==0 (L12), then e->name and e are freed (L13, 14), and the dereferencing e->name in audit_log (L16) leads to UAF (Fig. 1(d) ). By instructing the LLM to explicitly track and output these state changes, we transform natural language reasoning into a machine-readable schema that can be deterministically checked against the input source code.

paragraphs.en: Next, VERA performs reasoning auditing by evaluating the SRR through a multi-stage judge to detect reasoning breakdowns across a comprehensive taxonomy of fundamental failure modes (Step II). We define reasoning auditing as evaluating code adherence and internal consistency . The former refers to checking whether each claim in an LLM’s reasoning chain is syntactically and semantically supported by the provided source code slice ( Guo et al., 2026 ) ( e.g. , whether variables named in the trace are actually declared). The later refers to verifying that intermediate trace steps remain logically coherent and strictly support the final verdict ( e.g. , ensuring the final vulnerable verdict does not contradict the trace). Note that neither check requires ground-truth reasoning annotations which do not exist in real-world applications. Existing vulnerability validation techniques are fundamentally unsuited for this task. Benchmark studies evaluate only final detection metrics, treating internal reasoning as a black box ( Fan et al., 2020 ; Ding et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2023 ) . Traditional static tools ( Avgustinov et al., 2016 ; Yamaguchi et al., 2014 ; r2c / Semgrep Inc., 2024 ) focus on rule-based detection rather than explanatory auditability, frequently flooding triage queues with high false-positive rates without explaining root causes. Dynamic validation methods ( e.g. , fuzzing ( Fioraldi et al., 2020 ; Xia et al., 2024 ; Pham et al., 2019 ) or sanitizer-based execution ( Serebryany et al., 2012 ; Nethercote and Seward, 2007 ) ) and LLM-based vulnerability validation ( Guo et al., 2026 ; Zhu et al., 2026 ; Lu et al., 2026 ) have a fundamentally different goal from reasoning auditing. They confirm whether the detected bug exists or executes at runtime rather than whether the explanatory reasoning is sound. To remain broadly applicable across diverse programming languages and vulnerability classes (CWEs) without requiring language-specific static analyzers or heavy compilation toolchains, VERA’s judge relies primarily on deterministic AST parsing for syntactic checking, reserving targeted LLM calls strictly for higher-level semantic checks. By evaluating the SRR rather than unstructured text, VERA exposes both reasoning mistakes in the example: the omitted memory operations and the invalid assumption drawn from the stale comment.

paragraphs.en: In summary, this paper makes the following contributions. 1) VERA: A Reasoning Audit Framework for Vulnerability Analysis. VERA takes an initial step toward systematic LLM reasoning validation in software security by providing an automated framework to audit code adherence and internal consistency in vulnerability reasoning. 2) Automated Mutation Testing for Reasoning Judges. Evaluating reasoning evaluators has traditionally required unscalable human inspection. By formalizing reasoning into explicit, machine-readable SRRs, VERA enables automated, ground-truth-free mutation testing of reasoning judges, providing a scalable framework to automatically benchmark judge precision and recall without human spot-checks. 3) Empirical Findings & Practical Impact: Our experiments using VERA reveal three critical insights. First, reasoning flaws occur in correct verdicts just as frequently as incorrect ones, models are right for the wrong reasons as often as they are simply wrong, making reasoning audit necessary. Second, false positives are systematic and structure-driven: models repeat identical reasoning mistakes on safe functions and their patched variants. Third, VERA’s per-stage decomposition reveals code-structural patterns that drive specific reasoning failures. By surfacing failures as explicit stage-level findings, VERA reduces manual effort to audit LLM reasoning chains for security analysts and provides LLM developers with actionable diagnostics for targeted fine-tuning and benchmark design.

paragraphs.en: In this section, we motivate VERA through the poor performance of LLM-generated CoT vulnerability explanations, highlight the challenges of auditing LLM reasoning at scale, and describe how VERA addresses these challenges via SRR.
paragraphs.zh: 在本节中，我们将通过 LLM 生成的 CoT 漏洞解释表现不佳这一现象来阐述提出 VERA 的必要性，强调大规模审计 LLM 推理所面临的挑战，并说明 VERA 如何通过 SRR 应对这些挑战。

paragraphs.en: LLM analyses may rely on pattern matching, memorization, or hallucinated reasoning ( Lekssays et al., 2025 ; Geirhos et al., 2020 ; Pearce et al., 2022 ; Turpin et al., 2023 ; Lyu et al., 2023 ) . To evaluate reasoning validity, we manually audited free-form CoT explanations from four state-of-the-art LLMs on all 64 UAF vulnerable/patched function pairs in SVEN ( He and Vechev, 2023 ) (see supplementary material for details). Two human security experts audited each response across three dimensions: (1) verdict and CWE correctness, (2) factual accuracy of cited external knowledge (e.g., CVEs), and (3) the extent to which the reasoning was grounded in the code slice provided to the LLM as input. Our findings are three-fold, each illustrating a different way free-form CoT obscures reasoning mistakes that VERA is designed to surface.
paragraphs.zh: LLM 的分析可能依赖于模式匹配、记忆或幻觉推理（Lekssays 等人，2025；Geirhos 等人，2020；Pearce 等人，2022；Turpin 等人，2023；Lyu 等人，2023）。 为评估推理的有效性，我们手动审计了四种当前最先进的 LLM 在 SVEN 中全部 64 个 UAF 脆弱/已修复函数对上的自由形式 CoT 解释（He 和 Vechev，2023）（详见补充材料）。 两位人类安全专家从三个维度审计了每个响应：（1）判断结果和 CWE 的正确性；（2）所引用外部知识（例如 CVE）的事实准确性；以及（3）推理在多大程度上基于提供给 LLM 作为输入的代码片段。 我们的发现包括三个方面，每个方面都展示了自由形式 CoT 以不同方式掩盖推理错误的方式，而 VERA 正是为揭示这些错误而设计的。

paragraphs.en: First, despite achieving moderate binary accuracy ( 46 ​ – ​ 60 % 46\text{--}60\% ), models rarely identify the correct vulnerability type (true CWE recall is only 3 ​ – ​ 16 % 3\text{--}16\% ) and label both vulnerable and patched versions as VULNERABLE in up to 80 % 80\% of pairs. These numbers indicate widespread reasoning mistakes in the model’s explanation, yet free-form CoT poses challenges for auditing. Natural language imposes no structure on claims, allows contradictions to coexist with correct statements, and cannot be reliably parsed or checked. VERA addresses this by replacing free-form prose with an SRR that explicitly records every claimed memory operation, state transition, and property check. This state-transition-based explanation mirrors conceptually how human experts reason about and explain vulnerabilities, by tracing where an object is allocated, freed, and accessed again. With reasoning expressed in this structured form, the multi-stage judge can automatically locate and check each claim against the code slice.
paragraphs.zh: 首先，尽管模型在二元分类任务中取得了中等准确率（46%–60%），但它们很少能正确识别漏洞类型（真实 CWE 召回率仅为 3%–16%），并且在多达 80% 的样本对中，将存在漏洞和已修复的版本都标记为“存在漏洞”。 这些数据表明模型的解释中存在普遍的推理错误，但自由形式的 CoT 也给审计工作带来了挑战。 自然语言并未对陈述施加任何结构，允许矛盾陈述与正确陈述共存，并且无法被可靠地解析或验证。 VERA 通过用 SRR 替代自由形式的文本来解决这一问题，SRR 明确记录了所有声称的记忆操作、状态转换和属性检查。 这种基于状态转换的解释在概念上模拟了人类专家推理和解释漏洞的方式，即追踪对象被分配、释放以及再次访问的位置。 当推理以这种结构化形式呈现时，多阶段评判器就可以自动定位并针对代码片段验证每一项声称。

paragraphs.en: Second, examining the content of these errors more closely, we find that models frequently jump to conclusions by citing CVEs, bug reports, or domain conventions as justification rather than the code itself. Our manual review showed these claims are factually wrong 55 ​ – ​ 61 % 55\text{--}61\% of the time . For example, when analyzing the SVEN function kvm_ioctl_create_device , Sonnet-5 flagged both the vulnerable and patched versions as VULNERABLE while citing CVE-2019-6974—a reference-counting defect, not a UAF. Free-form CoT permits authoritative assertions (e.g., “This matches CVE-X” ) without mapping them to concrete code regions, which may trick both human reviewers and LLM judges. VERA detects this by validating each claim recorded in the SRR against the input code. A verdict citing CVE-2019-6974 must also record the corresponding pointer allocation, deallocation, and dereference in the code slice. A hallucinated citation will produce a trace with mistakes, and VERA flags the reasoning mistakes.
paragraphs.zh: 其次，通过更仔细地研究这些错误的内容，我们发现模型经常通过引用 CVE、错误报告或领域惯例作为依据来草率得出结论，而不是依据代码本身。 我们的手动审查表明，这些断言在 55%–61% 的情况下实际上是错误的。 例如，在分析 SVEN 函数 kvm_ioctl_create_device 时，Sonnet-5 将易受攻击和已修复的版本都标记为“存在漏洞”，同时引用了 CVE-2019-6974——这是一个引用计数缺陷，而非 UAF。 自由形式的 CoT 允许提出权威性的断言（例如，“这与 CVE-X 匹配”），而无需将其映射到具体的代码区域，这可能会误导人类评审员和 LLM 裁判。 VERA 通过验证 SRR 中记录的每一项断言与输入代码的对应关系来检测这一问题。 任何引用 CVE-2019-6974 的判断结果都必须同时记录代码片段中相应的指针分配、释放和解引用操作。 虚构的引用会产生包含错误的追踪记录，而 VERA 会标记出这些推理错误。

paragraphs.en: Third, across all models, 19 ​ – ​ 34 % 19\text{--}34\% of responses relied on ungrounded assertions about callee behaviors or domain conventions, which is not part of the input to LLMs. For instance, when analyzing disk_seqf_stop , Sonnet-5 declared the slice NOT VULNERABLE by asserting that “the stop callback is always called with a valid seqf—this is an accepted kernel convention.” In unstructured text, such premises are embedded into text, making it impossible to separate facts from speculative assumptions. VERA makes such assumptions explicit by encoding callee behavior and domain conventions as separate SRR fields, enabling judges to verify or reject them.

paragraphs.en: In this section, we present the key components underlying VERA’s reasoning audit framework. We first model vulnerabilities as sequences of state transitions within program slices (Sec. 3.1 ). This representation closely mirrors conceptually how human security experts reason about and explain vulnerabilities, and forms the foundation of the Structured Reasoning Record (SRR) schema (Sec. 3.2 ). The SRR is designed to externalize implicit LLM reasoning into a collection of inspectable facts. Finally, we introduce a failure taxonomy comprising eight fundamental reasoning error types, each corresponding to errors that may arise within SRR blocks (Sec. 3.3 ).
paragraphs.zh: 在本节中，我们介绍了 VERA 推理审计框架的核心组成部分。 首先，我们将漏洞建模为程序切片内的状态转换序列（第 3.1 节）。 这种表示方式在概念上高度模拟了人类安全专家对漏洞的推理和解释过程，并构成了结构化推理记录（SRR）模式的基础（第 3.2 节）。 SRR 的设计旨在将隐式的 LLM 推理外显化为一组可检查的事实。 最后，我们引入了一种故障分类体系，包含八种基本的推理错误类型，每种类型都对应 SRR 块中可能出现的错误（第 3.3 节）。

paragraphs.en: Following prior works that model program behavior as state transition systems and software vulnerabilities as sequences of state transitions that reach a bad state ( Lamport, 1977 ; Ball and Rajamani, 2002 ; Engler et al., 2000 ; Schneider, 2000 ; Cheng et al., 2024 ; Strom and Yemini, 1986 ) , we specify software vulnerabilities using state-based definitions. For example, a use-after-free (UAF) vulnerability is characterized by a sequence of allocation, release, and access operations on a resource, where each operation transitions the resource to a new state. The vulnerability manifests when the resource is dereferenced after it has entered the FREED state ( Cheng et al., 2024 ) . The informal definitions for CWEs of concern are shown below.
paragraphs.zh: 先前的研究将程序行为建模为状态转换系统，并将软件漏洞建模为导致不良状态的一系列状态转换（Lamport, 1977；Ball and Rajamani, 2002；Engler et al., 2000；Schneider, 2000；Cheng et al., 2024；Strom and Yemini, 1986），我们则使用基于状态的定义来描述软件漏洞。 例如，使用后释放（UAF）漏洞的特征是：对某个资源执行分配、释放和访问操作的一系列过程，其中每次操作都会使该资源进入一个新的状态。 当该资源在进入“已释放”（FREED）状态之后被解引用时，漏洞便会显现（Cheng et al., 2024）。 相关CWE的非正式定义如下所示。

paragraphs.en: This specification captures heap-memory lifecycle transitions. A heap resource M M is accessed through one or more pointer handles p p , where reachability depends on the existence of a handle in scope. State changes are induced by operations (e.g., 𝚊𝚕𝚕𝚘𝚌 \mathtt{alloc} and 𝚏𝚛𝚎𝚎 \mathtt{free} ). The aliasing rule ensures that any alternate pointer x x referencing M M inherits its state ( Fink et al., 2006 ) . Use-after-free accesses a resource in the FREED state. Double free attempts to release it a resource in the FREED state. A memory leak occurs when the resource becomes unreachable while the resource remains in ALLOC state.
paragraphs.zh: 本规范描述了堆内存的生命周期状态转换。 堆资源 M M 通过一个或多个指针句柄 p p 访问，其可达性取决于作用域内是否存在该句柄。 状态变化由操作（例如 𝚊𝚕𝚕𝚘𝚌 \mathtt{alloc} 和 𝚏𝚛𝚎𝚎 \mathtt{free}）引发。 别名规则确保任何引用 M M 的替代指针 x x 都会继承其状态（Fink et al., 2006）。 使用后释放操作访问处于 FREED 状态的资源。 双重释放尝试释放处于 FREED 状态的资源。 当资源变为不可达但仍处于 ALLOC 状态时，会发生内存泄漏。

sents.en: This specification captures heap-memory lifecycle transitions.
sents.zh: 本规范描述了堆内存的生命周期状态转换。

sents.en: A heap resource M M is accessed through one or more pointer handles p p , where reachability depends on the existence of a handle in scope.
sents.zh: 堆资源 M M 通过一个或多个指针句柄 p p 访问，其可达性取决于作用域内是否存在该句柄。

sents.en: State changes are induced by operations (e.g., 𝚊𝚕𝚕𝚘𝚌 \mathtt{alloc} and 𝚏𝚛𝚎𝚎 \mathtt{free} ).
sents.zh: 状态变化由操作（例如 𝚊𝚕𝚕𝚘𝚌 \mathtt{alloc} 和 𝚏𝚛𝚎𝚎 \mathtt{free}）引发。

sents.en: The aliasing rule ensures that any alternate pointer x x referencing M M inherits its state ( Fink et al., 2006 ) .
sents.zh: 别名规则确保任何引用 M M 的替代指针 x x 都会继承其状态（Fink et al., 2006）。

sents.en: Use-after-free accesses a resource in the FREED state.
sents.zh: 使用后释放操作访问处于 FREED 状态的资源。

sents.en: Double free attempts to release it a resource in the FREED state.
sents.zh: 双重释放尝试释放处于 FREED 状态的资源。

sents.en: A memory leak occurs when the resource becomes unreachable while the resource remains in ALLOC state.
sents.zh: 当资源变为不可达但仍处于 ALLOC 状态时，会发生内存泄漏。

paragraphs.en: This state-transition formulation generalizes naturally to stateful resource abstractions following open–use–close or state-gated patterns, such as network sockets, database connections, or session authentication states. Other natural extensions include, pointer validity, general resource releases, file descriptors, and object initialization (see definitions in supplementary material). Extending the framework to additional CWEs requires specifying their resource states, state-relevant operations, and violation conditions, alongside updating the reasoning schema and auditor rules.

paragraphs.en: Standard free-text reasoning hides reasoning errors within fluent prose ( Lekssays et al., 2025 ; Geirhos et al., 2020 ; Pearce et al., 2022 ; Turpin et al., 2023 ; Lyu et al., 2023 ) , rendering automated verification impossible. Based on state-transition-based vulnerability specifications, VERA requires the target detection model to structure its analysis into four linked blocks (Step I of Fig. 1(b) ): scope and alias sets (Block 1), state traces along execution paths (Block 2), property evaluations (Block 3), and the final verdict (Block 4). Crucially, each block records the model’s claims . We demonstrate with the example in Fig. 1 , the SRR is shown in Fig. 2 .
paragraphs.zh: 标准的自由文本推理将推理错误隐藏在流畅的论述中（Lekssays 等，2025；Geirhos 等，2020；Pearce 等，2022；Turpin 等，2023；Lyu 等，2023），使得自动化验证成为不可能。 基于状态转换的漏洞规范，VERA 要求目标检测模型将其分析结构化地分为四个相互关联的模块（图 1(b) 的步骤 I）：作用域和别名集（模块 1）、执行路径上的状态轨迹（模块 2）、属性评估（模块 3）以及最终判定（模块 4）。 关键在于，每个模块都会记录模型的断言。 我们通过图 1 中的示例进行演示，SRR 如圖 2 所示。

paragraphs.en: Block 1 (Scope): Captures declared entities, including relevant variables, assumed initial states, observed operations, and alias equivalence sets. In our running example (Fig. 2 ), the model identifies pointer e with initial state ALLOC and lists operations cache_lookup , cache_remove , and e->refs , missing key free operations. This block can be viewed as the definitions of variables and operations in the explanation. Block 2 (Trace of State Changes): Records the model’s path-sensitive reasoning as an explicit sequence: which operations occur, along which execution paths, in what order, and with what state transitions. In Fig. 2 , the model asserts that P 0 P_{0} executes unconditionally and branches at if (!e) into P 1 P_{1} and P 2 P_{2} , then logs the resulting state changes. Because the model incorrectly assumes cache_remove releases e , it records an incorrect transition from ALLOC to FREED on P 1 P_{1} — a reasoning mistake now expressed as an explicit field that can be inspected and checked. Block 3 (CWE Property Audit): Records explicit per-CWE safety claims.

paragraphs.en: By structuring intermediate reasoning into discrete, typed fields, the schema makes LLM vulnerability analyses auditable and surfaces errors as concrete, verifiable claims.
paragraphs.zh: 通过将中间推理结构化为离散且带类型的字段，该模式使大型语言模型（LLM）的漏洞分析具备可审计性，并能将错误以具体、可验证的断言形式呈现出来。

paragraphs.en: To systematically identify LLM reasoning errors as presented in SRR, we derive a taxonomy of eight fundamental reasoning failure modes ( F 1 F_{1} – F 8 F_{8} ), see Tbl. 2 . These failure modes correspond to the state-based definition and the SRR schema: the tracked resources and active handles, the valid state transitions, the paths containing those transitions, and the violation conditions. Hence, our taxonomy is organized across four core reasoning dimensions: 1) Lexical and evidence integrity ( F 1 , F 2 F_{1},F_{2} ), whether all relevant variables, pointers, and initial states are correctly scoped and that every claimed fact is anchored to concrete source operations rather than external assumptions or identifier naming conventions; 2) State correctness ( F 3 , F 4 , F 5 F_{3},F_{4},F_{5} ), whether state transitions accurately match witnessed source operations, that alias relations are tracked and state mutations propagated across all co-referencing handles ( Fink et al., 2006 ) , and that intermediate state changes are completely recorded without omissions; 3) Path validity ( F 6 , F 7 F_{6},F_{7} ), whether state transitions occur along valid, connected execution paths, requiring these paths to be syntactically connected from entry to the transition point, with branch conditions faithfully drawn from source rather than fabricated branches or statically dead code; and 4) Output coherence ( F 8 F_{8} ), whether the final security verdict strictly follows from step-by-step property evaluations without logical self-contradictions ( Turpin et al., 2023 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 为了系统性地识别 SRR 中呈现的 LLM 推理错误，我们构建了一个包含八种基本推理失败模式（F₁–F₈）的分类体系，参见表 2。 这些失败模式对应于基于状态的定义和 SRR 框架：被跟踪的资源与活动句柄、有效的状态转换、包含这些转换的路径，以及违反条件。 因此，我们的分类体系围绕四个核心推理维度展开：1）词汇与证据完整性（F₁、F₂），即所有相关变量、指针和初始状态是否被正确限定作用域，且每个声称的事实是否都锚定在具体的源操作上，而非外部假设或标识符命名惯例；2）状态正确性（F₃、F₄、F₅），即状态转换是否准确匹配观测到的源操作、别名关系是否被跟踪且状态变化是否在所有共引用句柄中传播（Fink 等，2006），以及中间状态的变化是否被完整记录而无遗漏；3）路径有效性（F₆、F₇），即状态转换是否沿着有效且相连的执行路径发生，要求这些路径从入口到转换点具有语法上的连通性，且分支条件必须忠实源自源代码，而非虚构的分支或静态死代码；以及 4）输出一致性（F₈），即最终的安全判定是否严格遵循逐步的属性评估过程，而不存在逻辑自相矛盾（Turpin 等，2023）。

paragraphs.en: After the detection model outputs an SRR, VERA evaluates it using the multi-stage judge shown in Step II of Fig. 1(b) . The judge performs a claim validation : it checks whether the model’s explicit reasoning claims are grounded in the input code and internally coherent. The multi-stage judge contains eight stages (S1–S8), each targeting one failure mode ( F 1 F_{1} – F 8 F_{8} from Tbl. 2 ). The stages follow a logical dependency chain: S1–S2 establish scope; S3–S4 validate path structure against the declared scope; S5–S6 check state transitions against the established scope and paths; S7 verifies alias propagation across the full trace; and S8 checks verdict coherence against all prior findings.

paragraphs.en: S1 (deterministic): Checking for Scope Error ( F 1 F_{1} ). Stage S1 checks Block 1 against the source code AST to verify the completeness and accuracy of the declared scope. Using Tree-Sitter, VERA extracts two ground-truth sets: cwe-relevant variables (i.e., memory-related variables such as pointers and fields for memory CWEs, and resource-related variables such as file descriptor for resource CWEs) and state-relevant operations (e.g., allocations, deallocations, dereferences for memory CWEs, acquire and release for resource CWEs). First, we check for scope hallucination and completeness, every variable and operation claimed in Block 1 exist in the input code slice, and all variables and operations in the code slices must exist in the declared scope in Block 1. Operations hidden inside missing callee context are flagged with a MISSING_CONTEXT warning. In Block 1 of Fig. 2 , S1 would flags the missing deallocation operations on L13–14 and the missing dereference on L16 as scope incompleteness errors. Additionally, initial state declarations in Block 1 must comply with C memory initialization rules: claiming ALLOCATED or FREED for a local variable before any corresponding operation appears in the slice is flagged as a scope error. Function parameters are an exception: when caller context is absent from the slice, their initial states cannot be checked hence not flagged as a scope error but a MISSING_CONTEXT warning.
paragraphs.zh: S1（确定性）：检查作用域错误（F 1 F_{1}）。 阶段 S1 将块 1 与源代码 AST 进行比对，以验证所声明作用域的完整性和准确性。 VERA 使用 Tree-Sitter 提取两个基准事实集合：CWE 相关的变量（即与内存相关的变量，如指针和字段，用于内存类 CWE；以及与资源相关的变量，如文件描述符，用于资源类 CWE）和状态相关的操作（例如，内存类 CWE 中的分配、释放和解引用操作；资源类 CWE 中的获取和释放操作）。 首先，我们检查是否存在作用域幻觉以及作用域是否完整：块 1 中声明的每个变量和操作都必须存在于输入代码片段中，且代码片段中的所有变量和操作都必须存在于块 1 所声明的作用域内。 隐藏在未提供调用者上下文中的操作会被标记为 MISSING_CONTEXT 警告。 在图 2 的块 1 中，S1 会将 L13–14 处缺失的释放操作以及 L16 处缺失的解引用操作标记为作用域不完整错误。 此外，块 1 中的初始状态声明必须遵循 C 语言内存初始化规则：如果在代码片段中出现任何对应的操作之前，就声称某个局部变量为 ALLOCATED 或 FREED，则会被标记为作用域错误。 函数参数是一个例外：当调用者上下文未包含在代码片段中时，其初始状态无法被检查，因此不会被标记为作用域错误，而是作为 MISSING_CONTEXT 警告处理。

paragraphs.en: S2 (LLM): Check for Assumptions ( F 2 F_{2} ). Stage S2 takes Block 1 and Block 2 together with the input code slice and uses targeted LLM calls to check whether any claims rely on hidden or external assumptions ungrounded in the code. For each claim, a targeted LLM call evaluates whether the provided justification is backed strictly by evidence explicitly present in the reasoning record and source code slice. In Fig. 2 , S2 will flag the claim that cache_remove releases e as an ungrounded external assumption since no deallocation operation on e exist in the code slice. This step deploys LLM because detecting implicit natural-language assumptions in justifications is an irreducibly semantic task that cannot be resolved via deterministic parsing.
paragraphs.zh: S2（LLM）：检查假设（F 2 F_{2}）。 S2 阶段将 Block 1 和 Block 2 与输入代码片段结合，并通过定向 LLM 调用检查任何主张是否依赖代码中无依据的隐藏或外部假设。 对于每个主张，定向 LLM 调用会评估所提供的理由是否严格由推理记录和源代码片段中明确存在的证据支持。 在图 2 中，S2 会将“cache_remove 释放 e”这一主张标记为无依据的外部假设，因为代码片段中不存在对 e 的释放操作。 此步骤采用 LLM，因为检测理由中隐含的自然语言假设是一项本质上具有语义性的任务，无法通过确定性解析解决。

paragraphs.en: S4 (deterministic): Check for Dead Code Reliance ( F 7 F_{7} ). Stage S4 checks Block 2’s trace against the source AST to detect whether any claimed state transitions are grounded in syntactically unexecutable code. S4 targets syntactically detectable dead code (e.g., if (0) , while (false) ) — the subset reliably identifiable with static analysis on a code slice alone. More accurate dead-code detection would require CFG construction and is left for future work.

paragraphs.en: S5 (deterministic): Check for Trace Coverage ( F 5 F_{5} ). Stage S5 cross-checks Block 2’s execution trace against the declared operations in Block 1 to enforce internal consistency. While S1 grounds Block 1 against the source code, S5 ensures the model does not cherry-pick supporting operations in its trace while silently omitting contradicting ones. To avoid false positives, VERA restricts this check to variables actively tracked in the trace: S5 flags a gap only when a model traces a variable but omits a confirmed operation on that same variable. For instance, if the model traces pointer p through allocation and dereference but skips an intermediate free(p) call, S5 flags the omission—as that missing operation determines whether the pattern constitutes a Use-After-Free. As illustrated in Fig. 2 , S5 does not re-flag ungrounded operations already caught by S1, focusing strictly on trace-completeness gaps.
paragraphs.zh: S5（确定性）：检查轨迹覆盖性（F 5 F_{5}）。 S5 阶段将 Block 2 的执行轨迹与 Block 1 中声明的操作进行交叉验证，以确保内部一致性。 虽然 S1 将 Block 1 与源代码进行对照验证，但 S5 确保模型不会在轨迹中挑选性地保留支持性操作，同时悄无声息地忽略矛盾操作。 为避免误报，VERA 将此检查限制在轨迹中主动跟踪的变量上：仅当模型追踪了某个变量却遗漏了对该变量的确认操作时，S5 才会标记出缺失环节。 例如，如果模型追踪了指针 p 的分配和解引用过程，但跳过了中间的 free(p) 调用，S5 就会标记这一遗漏——因为这一缺失操作决定了该模式是否构成“使用后释放”问题。 如图 2 所示，S5 不会重新标记已被 S1 捕获的未验证操作，而是严格专注于轨迹完整性的缺失环节。

paragraphs.en: S6 (deterministic): Check for State Transition ( F 3 F_{3} ). Stage S6 checks every state transition in Block 2 against the source code and CWE state-based definition to verify correctness and ordering. For every state transition in Block 2, Stage S6 deterministically checks whether the state update complies with the transitions defined in the state-based definitions, e.g., transitioning to FREED on a free operation; and whether the ordering of transitions is consistent with the input code slice. Additionally, for resource leaks (CWE-401 and CWE-772), an end-of-trace check verifies whether allocated variables remain in an unreleased state at the end of the function. In Fig. 2 , S6 flags the ALLOC to FREED transition attributed to cache_remove , since no deallocation semantics are established for that call.
paragraphs.zh: S6（确定性）：检查状态转换（F 3 F_{3}）。 S6 阶段会对照源代码和 CWE 基于状态的定义，验证块 2 中每个状态转换的正确性和顺序。 对于块 2 中的每个状态转换，S6 阶段都会确定性地检查状态更新是否符合基于状态的定义中规定的转换（例如，在执行自由操作时转换到 FREED），以及转换顺序是否与输入代码片段一致。 此外，针对资源泄漏（CWE-401 和 CWE-772），追踪结束检查会验证分配变量在函数结束时是否仍处于未释放状态。 在图 2 中，S6 标记了由 cache_remove 引起的从 ALLOC 到 FREED 的转换，因为该调用尚未建立释放语义。

paragraphs.en: S7 (LLM): Check for Alias ( F 4 F_{4} ). Stage S7 takes Block 1 and Block 2 together with the source slice and uses a targeted LLM call to evaluate whether alias relationships are correctly identified and state mutations propagated to all coreferencing aliases. For example, if p is freed and q = p , then both p and q should be in the FREED state. paragraphs.en: Final Judge Outcome. Upon executing all eight stages, VERA classifies the reasoning record into one of four final outcomes. (1) NO_ERROR : All stages pass without hard failures, indicating the reasoning chain is complete, internally consistent, and grounded in the input code slice. (2) MINOR_ERRORS : At least one stage triggers a warning without hard failures (e.g., unverifiable callee context or unconfirmed aliases). The core reasoning chain remains valid, but requires targeted review of the claims that triggered the warning. (3) MAJOR_ERRORS : At least one stage triggers a hard failure ( F 1 F_{1} – F 8 F_{8} ), such as a claimed dereference absent from the code slice ( F 3 F_{3} ), an inverted allocation–free sequence ( F 4 F_{4} ), or a verdict inconsistent with property checks ( F 7 F_{7} ). VERA reports the specific stage and offending claim involved. Human security analysts can use these localized diagnostics to quickly audit suspicious code regions without reading full traces, while downstream LLMs can ingest these targeted error reports to drive self-correction loops or filter unreliable verdicts. Crucially, a correct binary verdict and MAJOR_ERRORS can co-occur, exposing instances where a model reached the right answer through fabricated reasoning. (4) INCOMPLETE_RECORD : The model failed to generate a parseable reasoning record, excluded from reasoning-quality evaluation and flagged for re-query.

paragraphs.en: Evaluating the Judge via Mutation Testing. Assessing the reliability of reasoning judges requires ground-truth reasoning errors ( Zhu et al., 2026 ) , which is hard to obtain. Human review of individual reasoning chains is expensive and does not scale. One approach to acquire ground-truth data at scale in software testing without human annotation is mutation testing, which generates mutants with errors injected ( Doddapaneni et al., 2024 ; Delcourt et al., 2026 ) . While this approach does not transfer directly to natural language reasoning, VERA’s SRR can be programmatically injected with precise, category-controlled faults. For example, deleting a state transition ( F 3 F_{3} ), severing an alias link ( F 4 F_{4} ), or fabricating an execution path ( F 6 F_{6} ) can produce exact ground-truth errors. VERA thus supports automated mutation-based evaluation of judges across the full failure taxonomy ( F 1 F_{1} – F 8 F_{8} ), enabling rigorous, scalable stress testing of reasoning judges operating on SRRs.

paragraphs.en: Scope and Limitations. To enable language-agnostic, build-free deployment at scale, VERA’s judge operates directly on uncompiled code slices without requiring whole-program build environments. This design choice imposes two main operational boundaries. First, implicit operations introduced through type casts, struct field accesses, or opaque callees require type-system reasoning beyond AST-level pattern matching. Consequently, the completeness check in S1 is scoped to statically verifiable operations — explicit calls to known C/C++ memory functions (e.g., malloc , free , realloc ); implicit operations are conservatively treated as warnings rather than hard failures. This is a deliberate trade-off that preserves zero false positives on structural checks at the cost of moderate recall in Stages S1 and S5. Second, checks that fundamentally require whole-program compilation, such as precise dead-code detection, alias resolution beyond direct pointer assignment, and formal path reachability, are currently outside VERA’s current scope. These are fundamental boundaries of intra-procedural auditing; integration with whole-program control-flow and points-to solvers is a natural direction for future work.

paragraphs.en: We evaluate VERA and answer the following questions. To establish that our error taxonomy is empirically grounded, we check that the failure categories reflect errors that occur in real LLM reasoning and answer: ( RQ1 ) Do the failure categories in our taxonomy reflect real LLM reasoning failures? Next, with the taxonomy established, we evaluate the effectiveness of VERA’s judge in detecting these errors. Since no ground-truth labels exist for reasoning errors, we use mutation testing to inject known errors into valid reasoning records, enabling precise, controlled evaluation of judge effectiveness. We answer ( RQ2 ) How does VERA’s multi-stage hybrid judge compare to a stage-structured LLM-as-a-judge in detecting reasoning errors? Finally, having established that VERA reliably detects reasoning errors, we then apply it at scale to real LLM reasoning traces to identify systematic reasoning failures, including “correct verdict, flawed reasoning”. We compare against free-form CoT baselines and answer: (RQ3) What systematic reasoning failures does VERA expose that binary accuracy metrics and free-form CoT judges fail to detect?"

sents.zh: 为了证明我们的错误分类体系具有经验依据，我们验证其故障类别是否反映了真实 LLM 推理中出现的错误，并回答：(RQ1) 我们分类体系中的故障类别是否反映了真实的 LLM 推理失败？

sents.en: Next, with the taxonomy established, we evaluate the effectiveness of VERA’s judge in detecting these errors.
sents.zh: 接下来，在分类体系确立后，我们评估 VERA 的判定器在检测这些错误方面的有效性。

sents.en: Since no ground-truth labels exist for reasoning errors, we use mutation testing to inject known errors into valid reasoning records, enabling precise, controlled evaluation of judge effectiveness.
sents.zh: 由于推理错误没有真实标签，我们采用变异测试方法将已知错误注入有效的推理记录中，从而能够精确、可控地评估判定器的有效性。

sents.en: We answer ( RQ2 ) How does VERA’s multi-stage hybrid judge compare to a stage-structured LLM-as-a-judge in detecting reasoning errors?
sents.zh: 我们回答：(RQ2) 与分阶段结构的 LLM 作为判定器相比，VERA 的多阶段混合判定器在检测推理错误方面的表现如何？

sents.en: Finally, having established that VERA reliably detects reasoning errors, we then apply it at scale to real LLM reasoning traces to identify systematic reasoning failures, including “correct verdict, flawed reasoning”.
sents.zh: 最后，在确认 VERA 能够可靠检测推理错误后，我们将其大规模应用于真实的 LLM 推理轨迹，以识别系统性的推理失败，包括“判定正确但推理存在缺陷”的情况。

sents.en: We compare against free-form CoT baselines and answer: (RQ3) What systematic reasoning failures does VERA expose that binary accuracy metrics and free-form CoT judges fail to detect?"
sents.zh: 我们将它与自由形式的 CoT 基线方法进行比较，并回答：(RQ3) VERA 揭示了哪些系统性的推理失败，而二元准确率指标和自由形式的 CoT 判定器却未能检测出来？

paragraphs.en: Datasets. We include paired datasets to evaluate whether stage-level reasoning failures persist across a vulnerable function and its patched counterpart, motivated by our observation in Sec. 2 , exposing whether model errors are driven by code structure rather than vulnerability presence.

paragraphs.en: Evaluation Configurations. Because no prior vulnerability reasoning auditing system directly audits intermediate reasoning without relying solely on an LLM-as-judge, we establish four evaluation configurations to systematically isolate the contributions of two core design choices: reasoning format (free-Form CoT ( Wei et al., 2022 ) vs. structured SRR) and audit architecture (holistic LLM-as-judge ( Zheng et al., 2023 ) vs. stage-structured LLM vs. VERA’s multi-stage hybrid judge). 1) Free-form baseline B1 : Free-Form CoT + Holistic LLM Judge. The detection model is prompted for open-ended reasoning. A holistic LLM-as-a-judge inspects the full narrative without stage decomposition. 2) Free-form baseline B2 : Free-Form CoT + stage-structured LLM Judge. Same free-form detection output as B1, but the judge is prompted to evaluate reasoning explicitly with stages corresponding to the eight taxonomy categories. 3) LLM-as-judge baseline B3 : SRR + stage-structured LLM Judge. The detection model materializes its reasoning into VERA’s SRR, then audited purely via an LLM judge using the same stage-structured prompts as B2. 4) VERA : SRR + Multi-Stage Hybrid Judge. The detection model outputs an SRR schema, which is then audited by VERA’s multi-stage hybrid pipeline. We show the benefit of structured reasoning by comparing B1/B2 vs. VERA (RQ3), and show the effectiveness of our multi-stage judge by comparing B3 vs. VERA (RQ2).
paragraphs.zh: 评估配置。 由于目前尚无漏洞推理审计系统能够直接审计中间推理过程，而无需完全依赖“LLM作为裁判”的机制，因此我们建立了四种评估配置，以系统地分离两种核心设计选择所带来的贡献：推理格式（自由形式 CoT（Wei et al., 2022）与结构化 SRR）以及审计架构（整体式 LLM 作为裁判（Zheng et al., 2023）与分阶段结构化 LLM 或 VERA 的多阶段混合裁判）。1) 自由形式基线 B1：自由形式 CoT + 整体式 LLM 裁判。 检测模型被提示进行开放式推理。 整体式 LLM 作为裁判会检查完整的叙述过程，而不对推理进行分阶段拆解。2) 自由形式基线 B2：自由形式 CoT + 分阶段结构化 LLM 裁判。 检测输出的自由形式与 B1 相同，但裁判被提示以与八个分类类别相对应的阶段来明确评估推理过程。3) LLM 作为裁判的基线 B3：SRR + 分阶段结构化 LLM 裁判。 检测模型将推理结果具体化为 VERA 的 SRR，随后仅通过 LLM 裁判进行审计，并使用与 B2 相同的分阶段结构化提示。4) VERA：SRR + 多阶段混合裁判。 检测模型输出一个 SRR 框架，随后由 VERA 的多阶段混合流程进行审计。 我们通过比较 B1/B2 与 VERA（研究问题 3），展示了结构化推理的优势；并通过比较 B3 与 VERA（研究问题 2），展示了我们多阶段裁判的有效性。

paragraphs.en: Mutation-based Judge Evaluation. We designed 13 mutation operators mapped directly across our taxonomy stages (see Tbl. 3 ). Each operator targets the precise reasoning breakdown that a given stage is designed to catch. These operators are designed to simulate errors that naturally arise in LLM-generated structured reasoning records, e.g., variables that appear in the analysis but not in source, memory operations that are silently omitted, paths with vague or self-contradictory activation conditions, and alias relationships left untracked. We aim for completeness within each stage by covering both directions of error where applicable — for instance, hallucination (claiming absent elements) and omission (missing real ones) at S1, or missing trace steps and invalid path references at S5. Then, we measure detection performance with two metrics. Note that not all operators are applicable to all SRRs, e.g., no op identified M 2 M_{2} cannot be applied. Recall is the fraction of mutants targeting a specific stage that are correctly flagged as failures. False-positive rate (FP) is the fraction of mutants targeting a different stage that are incorrectly identified.
paragraphs.zh: 基于突变的法官评估。 我们设计了 13 个突变算子，这些算子直接映射到我们的分类体系各阶段（参见表 3）。 每个算子都针对特定阶段旨在检测的精确推理断裂点。 这些算子旨在模拟大型语言模型生成的结构化推理记录中自然出现的错误，例如：分析中出现但未在源数据中出现的变量、被静默省略的记忆操作、激活条件模糊或自相矛盾的路径，以及未被追踪的别名关系。 我们的目标是在每个阶段内实现完整性，即覆盖所有适用的双向错误——例如，在 S1 阶段涵盖幻觉（声称存在不存在的元素）和遗漏（漏掉真实存在的元素），或在 S5 阶段涵盖缺失的追溯步骤和无效的路径引用。 接着，我们通过两个指标来衡量检测性能。 请注意，并非所有算子都适用于所有的 SRR，例如，没有算子能够应用于 M 2 M_{2}。 召回率是指针对特定阶段的突变体中被正确标记为失败的占比。 假阳性率（FP）是指针对其他阶段的突变体中被错误识别的占比。

paragraphs.en: To answer RQ1 , we evaluate whether our taxonomy ( F 1 ​ – ​ F 8 F_{1}\text{--}F_{8} ) accurately captures naturally occurring reasoning errors and whether our mutation operators ( M 1 ​ – ​ M 8 M_{1}\text{--}M_{8} ) provide complete coverage over real-world failure modes. paragraphs.en: To answer RQ2, we randomly sampled 20 SRRs per dataset per CWE, applied each mutation operator (prioritizing No_ERROR , falling back to MINOR_ERROR ), and measured per-stage recall and false-positive (FP) rates across the resulting mutated records. paragraphs.zh: 为回答研究问题2（RQ2），我们按数据集和CWE分别随机抽取了20个SRR，应用了每种变异算子（优先使用No_ERROR，若不可行则退而使用MINOR_ERROR），并测量了由此产生的变异记录在各个阶段的召回率和误报率（FP）。 在评分时，未变异的基线记录中预先存在的错误被排除在外，以确保所测得的召回率能反映对注入故障的检测能力。 对于每个变异体，我们检查了判断器是否标记了该算子所针对的具体阶段。 我们将VERA与B3（SRR + 结构化LLM判断器）进行了比较，后者是其仅使用LLM的对应版本，后者虽对相同的八个阶段的SRR进行审计，但每个阶段都使用LLM进行判断。 表5报告了三种判断器模型下，两个判断器在三个数据集上针对相同CWE的记录汇总后的各阶段召回率和偏离目标的误报率；所有SRR均由Sonnet-5生成，该模型能产生结构最完整的记录，且所有判断器均在同一组变异体上进行评估。

paragraphs.en: Primarily deterministic stages (S1, S3–S6, S8). VERA matches or outperforms B3 (SRR + structured LLM judge) across all these stages while maintaining near-zero off-target FP. S3, S6, and S8 achieve perfect recall ( 1.00 1.00 ) with 0.00 0.00 FP across all CWEs. Across these stages, B3 with GPT-4.1 as judge achieves recall 0.10–0.75 with FP up to 0.16; B3 with DeepSeek achieves 0.22–0.91 in recall but at FP up to 0.38 on clean records. B3 with Mistral reaches near-perfect recall on most of these stages, but only because of overflagging incurring FP up to 0.26. The key pattern underlying VERA’s advantage is absence detection : the errors targeted by S5 (missing intermediate state changes) and S6 (omitted or misordered transitions) require noticing what is not in the trace rather than what is. Fluent surrounding prose masks these gaps for an LLM judge — VERA’s deterministic trace checks find them mechanically. S5 shows the largest gap overall: VERA 91.5% vs. B3 72.8%, with 22.8% of injected errors caught by VERA alone. S6 shows the same pattern (+16.7%). The one exception to VERA’s structural advantage is S1, where recall falls slightly short due to a deliberate precision-first trade-off (Sec. 4 ); even so, S1 matches B3 recall with lower FP on two of three judge models. Notably, S8 (verdict consistency) is the one stage where the gap nearly closes regardless of judge type — VERA 100%, B3 98.8% — because an explicit contradiction between the property block and the final verdict is detectable in any structured representation without absence reasoning. Beyond quantitative metrics, B3 (SRR + structured LLM) exhibits severe hallucination on clean records. With GPT-4.1, on the SMB2_read control record (Linux kernel, CWE-416 in SVEN), B3 issued a Fail on S3 with the finding: “Hallucinated State Transition: rsp and *buf step 12, 15.” No such transition exists in either the record or the source — B3 invented a violation on a sound reasoning chain. VERA correctly returned Pass .
paragraphs.zh: 主要为确定性阶段（S1、S3–S6、S8）。 在所有这些阶段中，VERA与B3（SRR + 结构化LLM判官）的表现一致或更优，同时保持接近零的离目标假阳性率。 S3、S6和S8在所有CWE上均实现了完美的召回率（1.00 1.00），且假阳性率为0.00 0.00。 在这些阶段中，使用GPT-4.1作为判官的B3实现的召回率为0.10–0.75，假阳性率最高可达0.16；而使用DeepSeek的B3召回率为0.22–0.91，但在干净记录上的假阳性率最高可达0.38。 使用Mistral的B3在这些阶段的大多数情况下实现了接近完美的召回率，但这仅仅是因为过度标记导致假阳性率最高达到0.26。 VERA优势背后的关键模式是“缺失检测”：S5（缺少中间状态变化）和S6（遗漏或顺序错误的转换）所针对的错误，需要识别痕迹中不存在的内容，而非存在的内容。 流畅的上下文文本会掩盖这些缺失部分，使LLM判官难以察觉——而VERA的确定性痕迹检查能够机械地发现它们。 S5总体上显示出最大的差距：VERA为91.5%，而 B3为72.8%，其中22.8%的注入错误仅由VERA检测出。 S6也呈现出相同的模式（+16.7%）。 VERA结构性优势的唯一例外是S1，其召回率因刻意优先追求精确性而略有不足（第4节）；即便如此，在三种判官模型中，S1仍有两种模型实现了与B3相当的召回率且假阳性率更低。 值得注意的是，S8（裁决一致性）是唯一一个无论判官类型如何，差距几乎消失的阶段——VERA为100%，B3为98.8%——因为属性块与最终裁决之间的明确矛盾，在任何结构化表示中都能被检测到，无需进行缺失推理。 除了定量指标外，B3（SRR + 结构化LLM）在干净记录上还表现出严重的幻觉问题。 在使用GPT-4.1时，针对SMB2_read控制记录（Linux内核，SVEN中的CWE-416），B3在S3阶段给出了“失败”判定，并指出：“幻觉状态转换：rsp和*buf步骤12、15。”但记录或源代码中并不存在这样的转换——B3在一个合理的推理链中凭空捏造了一个违规项。 VERA正确地返回了“通过”。

paragraphs.en: Free-form baselines vs. VERA. Overall, B1 (CoT + Holistic LLM) yields an 86.8 % 86.8\% false-negative rate on records where VERA identifies deterministic-stage errors, underscoring the inadequacy of free-form LLM evaluation. As shown in Tbl. 6(b) , B1 (CoT + Holistic LLM) flags substantially fewer errors than VERA across every stage presented, whereas B2 (CoT + Structured LLM) over-flags in almost all stages while missing errors in S8. Discrepancies are largest on stages requiring precise cross-section consistency (S3, S5, S6, S8). A representative example is disk_seqf_stop (SVEN CWE-416, Sonnet-5): the SRR explicitly assigns iter as NULL then dereferences it in the next step, yet marks CWE-476 as Satisfied . VERA’s S8 detects this contradiction mechanically; B1 (CoT + Holistic LLM) rates the same SRR error-free, stating “The analysis correctly describes the bug, tracing all relevant pointer/state paths.” A holistic LLM judge infers coherence from parts that sound correct rather than verifying mutual consistency — which is precisely what structured stage checks provide. LLM-as-a-judge is inherently prompt-sensitive and therefore unreliable ( Zhu et al., 2025 ) . As shown in Tbl. 6(c) , B1 (CoT + Holistic LLM) and B2 (CoT + Structured LLM) disagree significantly on the same CoT inputs, confirming that free-form judging lacks the consistency needed for reliable reasoning auditing.

paragraphs.en: Finding 2: LLM over-flag by pattern-matching, not by reasoning. Among 1,468 functions evaluated by all six models, 103 safe functions were wrongly labelled as vulnerable by every model, compared to only 37 real vulnerabilities missed by all models. VERA’s structured audit flagged a reasoning error in 98 % 98\% of these over-flagged safe functions, with S8 as the dominant failure ( 82 % 82\% ). This reflects a reliance on surface pattern matching observed in Sec. 2 , models flag safe functions for containing vulnerable-like structural cues, then hallucinate ungrounded traces to justify their premature Vulnerable verdict. Examining paired data confirms this. Across 777 paired (vulnerable, patched) functions, both versions trigger the same stage failure in 51.1 % 51.1\% of pairs at S1, 27.7 % 27.7\% at S6, and 56.9 % 56.9\% at S8 — and 32.3 % 32.3\% of pairs share the exact errors across all stages. The model makes the same structural reasoning mistakes regardless of whether the vulnerability is present, confirming that over-prediction is driven by code pattern rather than vulnerability-specific reasoning.

paragraphs.en: Finding 3: Incomplete slices cause models to hallucinate lifecycle evidence. While over-flagging and miss rates are comparable for most CWEs, CWE-772 (Missing Release) is a major outlier: models correctly flag 75 % 75\% of actual leaks (highest recall across CWEs), yet falsely flag 73 % 73\% of safe functions. This stems from a mismatch between CWE-772 violation and slice visibility. Unlike local properties like CWE-476, confirming a CWE-772 leak requires verifying that the resource reaches a release state on every exit path — including paths that continue beyond the slice boundary. When an explicit release is absent from the local slice, models tend to default to predicting a leak. VERA’s stage results makes this concrete: S5 (Trace Coverage) fails at 30.8 % 30.8\% for CWE-772 (vs. 17.6 % 17.6\% for CWE-476). Furthermore, S6 (State Transitions) fails at 58.2 % 58.2\% (vs. 38.6 % 38.6\% for CWE-476), due to hallucinated release operations ( nullify(image) claimed in the trace but absent from source) and misordered transitions. Across both stages, models exhibit the same failure mode: when crucial lifecycle context lies beyond the visible slice, models commit prematurely to a verdict and insert unsupported trace artifacts to bridge the gap. VERA detects these as code adherence failures and flags them for human follow-up. An analyst can then inspect the full codebase to determine whether the claimed operations exist outside the slice boundary.

paragraphs.en: Finding 5: Different LLMs make different reasoning mistakes. VERA surfaces distinct error profiles across detection models, offering actionable results for model selection. The most universal finding is S8: every model fails this stage at 50 − 69 % 50-69\% , revealing that reconciling reasoning with the final verdict is a systematic weakness across all current architectures — and one that B1 misses almost entirely (Tbl. 6(b) ). Beyond S8, models diverge: Sonnet-5 and Qwen achieve the lowest S3 and S5 error rates ( 13 − 22 % 13-22\% ) while Gemma struggles ( 33 − 34 % 33-34\% ); yet Gemma leads on S6 ( 23 % 23\% ) while Qwen and Sonnet-5 incur 43 − 47 % 43-47\% . This heterogeneity enables targeted refinement — identifying a model’s exact failure stage rather than optimizing blindly for binary accuracy — and principled selection: models stronger on path traversal (Sonnet-5, Qwen) for deep control-flow vulnerabilities; models stronger on local state transitions (Gemma) for use-after-free lifecycles.

paragraphs.en: In summary, VERA reveals that reasoning quality is not related to binary accuracy, uncovers cross-section inconsistencies and systematic over-prediction that free-form judges miss, and provides fine-grained model diagnostic profiles invisible to standard benchmarks. Thus, we answer RQ3.
paragraphs.zh: 总而言之，VERA 表明推理质量与二元准确性并无关联，揭示了截面不一致性和自由形式评估者未能发现的系统性过度预测问题，并提供了标准基准无法呈现的精细模型诊断特征。因此，我们回答了研究问题 3（RQ3）。

paragraphs.en: 1) Construct — training data contamination. Public benchmarks like SVEN and PrimeVul may have been exposed to LLMs during pre-training. Contamination could bias models toward memorized binary verdicts rather than genuine code analysis. We mitigated this with extra CVE data collected after the model training date, and observed no significant difference in reasoning error rates, suggesting contamination alone does not explain the failures observed. 2) External — CWE scope. Our evaluation covers five C/C++ memory and resource lifecycle CWEs, which are among the most exploited and hardest to detect vulnerability classes in practice. Extending VERA to other CWEs is left as future work. 3) Internal — structured format bias. VERA can only check what is explicitly recorded in the SRR. A model that produces sparse or underspecified output gives VERA fewer opportunities to detect errors, which may inflate its sound rate independent of actual reasoning quality. We observed this with smaller open-source models; in this study, the five frontier models we evaluate reliably adhere to the schema. 4) Internal- Mutation-judge Alignment. A potential concern is that our mutation operators ( M 1 ​ – ​ M 8 M_{1}\text{--}M_{8} ) target structural properties inherently favored by VERA’s deterministic checks over LLM judges. We mitigate this by grounding the operators in naturally occurring errors. RQ1’s open-ended annotation confirms that M 1 M_{1} – M 8 M_{8} directly instantiate the error categories ( F 1 F_{1} – F 8 F_{8} ) that arise in real, un-mutated LLM reasoning. The mutations are therefore representative of real failures, not constructions designed to favor VERA.

paragraphs.en: LLM-based vulnerability detection. Learning-based vulnerability detection has moved from neural models over program representations ( Zhou et al., 2019 ; Chakraborty et al., 2022 ; Zhang et al., 2026 ; Du et al., 2026b ; Su et al., 2024 ; Du et al., 2024 ) to large language models fine-tuned on code ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) , with recent systems adding knowledge retrieval ( Du et al., 2026a ) , code-graph guidance ( Lekssays et al., 2025 ) , or taint inference ( Li et al., 2025b ) . These systems optimize for detection accuracy; VERA is not a detector, it audits the reasoning that a detection model records in an SRR.

paragraphs.en: Validating LLM-found vulnerabilities. LLM-based vulnerability detection increasingly include validity check of their vulnerability reports. LLift ( Li et al., 2024 ) prompts an LLM to review its responses against a set of rules, LLMSAN ( Wang et al., 2024b ) discards reports whose recorded data-flow paths fail its checks; LLMDFA ( Wang et al., 2024a ) checks path feasibility with an SMT solver and RepoAudit ( Guo et al., 2025 ) asks the LLM to find contradictions among path conditions; BugScope ( Guo et al., 2026 ) checks feasibility and whether its assumptions are justified by the code solely through an LLM-as-judge; VulInstruct ( Zhu et al., 2026 ) and DAGVul ( Lu et al., 2026 ) check for correctness by comparing with ground truth information also with LLM-as-judge. These approaches ask whether a reported vulnerability is real; VERA checks the reasoning behind the verdict. These two goals are complementary to each other, a validator can confirm a bug exists; VERA can reveal whether the LLM found it for the right reasons.
paragraphs.zh: 验证大型语言模型发现的漏洞。 基于大型语言模型的漏洞检测方法越来越多地包含对其漏洞报告的真实性检查。 LLift（Li 等人，2024）会提示大型语言模型根据一组规则审查其响应；LLMSAN（Wang 等人，2024b）会丢弃那些记录的数据流路径未能通过检查的报告；LLMDFA（Wang 等人，2024a）会使用 SMT 求解器检查路径的可行性；而 RepoAudit（Guo 等人，2025）则会要求大型语言模型找出路径条件之间的矛盾之处；BugScope（Guo 等人，2026）仅通过“大型语言模型作为裁判”的方式，检查可行性及其假设是否由代码本身所证实；VulInstruct（Zhu 等人，2026）和 DAGVul（Lu 等人，2026）则通过与基准真实信息进行比较，同样借助“大型语言模型作为裁判”来验证正确性。 这些方法旨在判断所报告的漏洞是否真实存在；而 VERA 则会检查得出该结论的推理过程。 这两个目标是相互补充的：验证工具可以确认漏洞是否存在，而 VERA 则能揭示大型语言模型是否基于正确的理由发现了该漏洞。

paragraphs.en: Checking LLM reasoning. Prior work has examined the reasoning behind vulnerability verdicts, but all rely on free-form CoT and LLM-as-judge. Free-form CoT has been shown to be unreliable, including in general natural language tasks ( Turpin et al., 2023 ; Arcuschin et al., 2026 ) and specifically for code reasoning ( Ullah et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2025a ) . LLM judges are widely used to evaluate model outputs ( Zheng et al., 2023 ; Crupi et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025 ) , including for code generation and SE tasks ( Chen et al., 2025 ; Liu et al., 2026 ; Abdollahi et al., 2026 ; Crupi et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025 ) , despite being susceptible to superficial cues ( Moon et al., 2026 ) . Some vulnerability detection approaches attempt to check reasoning correctness, as mentioned before, VulInstruct ( Zhu et al., 2026 ) and DAGVul ( Lu et al., 2026 ) , but do so only by comparing generated reasoning against ground truth obtained through patches or human annotation using a holistic LLM-as-judge. VERA instead checks claimed scope, state transitions, and assumptions directly against the code slice, requiring no ground-truth annotations and enabling deterministic checks of a few reasoning failures.
paragraphs.zh: 检查 LLM 的推理过程。 先前的工作已经研究了漏洞判定背后的推理，但所有研究都依赖自由形式的 CoT 和作为评判者的 LLM。 已有研究表明自由形式的 CoT 并不可靠，这不仅体现在一般的自然语言任务中（Turpin 等人，2023；Arcuschin 等人，2026），在代码推理领域尤其如此（Ullah 等人，2024；Zhang 等人，2026；Li 等人，2025a）。 LLM 评判者被广泛用于评估模型输出（Zheng 等人，2023；Crupi 等人，2025；Wang 等人，2025），包括代码生成和软件工程任务（Chen 等人，2025；Liu 等人，2026；Abdollahi 等人，2026；Crupi 等人，2025；Wang 等人，2025），尽管它们容易受到表面线索的影响（Moon 等人，2026）。 如前所述，一些漏洞检测方法试图验证推理的正确性，例如 VulInstruct（Zhu 等人，2026）和 DAGVul（Lu 等人，2026），但它们仅通过将生成的推理与通过补丁或人类标注获得的基准真相进行比较来实现，且依赖整体性的 LLM 作为评判者。 相比之下，VERA 直接针对代码片段验证所声称的作用域、状态转换和假设，无需基准真相标注，并能对少数推理错误进行确定性检查。

paragraphs.en: Evaluating reasoning judges. Most prior work evaluates vulnerability detectors against labeled ground-truth datasets. However, no such labels exist for reasoning quality, making judge evaluation significantly harder. Prior work evaluates judges on non-coding tasks by introducing predefined quality mutations into model outputs: FBI ( Doddapaneni et al., 2024 ) mutates natural language output quality (e.g., coherence and fluency) against checklist criteria, and Delcourt et al. ( Delcourt et al., 2026 ) mutate UML diagrams by injecting structural defects. This does not directly transfer to code reasoning: a meaningful mutation must identify a specific claim to modify, ensure it is wrong with respect to the source code, and attach a known failure category, but free-form CoT provides no clear anchors for any of these. VERA enables this by combining the SRR, which provides explicit claim boundaries and source grounding, with the failure taxonomy that defines typed failure categories to mutate.

paragraphs.en: This paper presented VERA, a framework for automated auditing of LLM vulnerability reasoning that replaces free-form LLM-as-judges with a deterministic/LLM pipeline over machine-readable Structured Reasoning Records. Our evaluation shows that reasoning quality is decoupled from verdict correctness: LLMs are frequently right for the wrong reasons, and this goes undetected by standard accuracy metrics and pure LLM-as-judges alike — LLM-as-judges miss 87 % 87\% of the reasoning flaws VERA detects mechanically. VERA’s per-stage decomposition further reveals structural correlates of reasoning failures invisible to binary accuracy: loop-heavy functions concentrate trace coverage errors, while null-heavy pointer patterns drive verdict inconsistencies. In practice, a security analyst using an LLM-based vulnerability scanner can run VERA to filter hallucinated reports before acting on them, while LLM developers can use its stage-wise failure profiles as targeted fine-tuning signals. Future work will extend VERA beyond C/C++ memory vulnerabilities to semantic flaw classes, integrate interprocedural static analysis to improve pointer alias recall, and leverage VERA’s stage-wise diagnostics as fine-grained training signals for LLM alignment.
